# Intake Brief: Achievement give-aways — unlock three games when achievements are achieved

## Problem statement

To reward engaged players, three games from the TCE catalog will be given away free when players achieve certain achievements in the Steam launcher. The unlock uses the **same game-agnostic mechanism** as the free game awarded for following on Steam (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC): bundled content locked by default, unlocked in place, persisted across launches.

## Users

- **Steam players** — earn free games as a reward for reaching achievements; a reason to keep playing.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — a growth/engagement mechanic that drives play without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want a free game to unlock in my launcher once I've won my first game and reached one more milestone, so my progress is rewarded.
- As a publisher, I want achievement give-aways delivered through the existing bundled-content/unlock architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Three games are selected** from the TCE catalog for achievement give-away; the selection is a documented business decision (Main Street is a noted candidate; selection avoids overlap with the follow-on-Steam bonus game choice — see Related work) and the chosen set + rationale is recorded in the item/design doc.
2. Each give-away game unlocks when the player achieves its configured trigger achievements: **"win your first game" plus one additional achievement** (suggested: first win in a second distinct game — final choice recorded, see Appendix). Trigger definitions live in one config (achievement ids → game id) and are game-agnostic.
3. The unlock uses **the same mechanism as the follow-on-Steam free game** (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC): bundled content, locked by default, unlocked in place, persisted across launches, game-agnostic unlock logic.
4. Unlock state persists across launches; re-checks on demand; graceful degradation when Steam/Steamworks is absent (CTA/lock state degrades without crashing the app).
5. Trigger achievements come from the engine-generic achievement layer (CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ): give-away config consumes achievement-unlock events, not game-specific hacks.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Reuse, don't reinvent:** the unlock mechanism (bundled-content unlock, persistence, game-agnostic design) is the one designed in CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC; this item adds achievement-triggered unlocks as an additional trigger source on the same path.
- **Game selection is a business decision** and part of this item's scope (user: "don't know yet (note Main Street)").
- **Dependencies:** blocked by CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ (achievements exist as engine-generic events) and CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC (unlock mechanism). Both are prerequisites for implementation.
- **Trigger achievements:** "win your first game" plus one more (user decision; second achievement suggested — final choice to be confirmed).
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).

## Existing state

- Follow-on-Steam item (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC, intake_complete) designs the game-agnostic free-game unlock: Steamworks-based follow detection + local unlock persistence + bundled DLC content; **not yet implemented** — this item should coordinate so the unlock path is shared.
- No achievement system exists yet; CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ (challenges → Steam achievements, engine-generic) is the event source this item consumes.
- Game catalog (`main.ts` GAMES): Gym (demos), 9-Card Golf, Beleaguered Castle, Sushi Go!, Feudalism, Lost Cities, Main Street, Blackjack, Coloretto. Steam launcher (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) will bundle a subset with DLC architecture.
- CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC has an open question: which game is the designated free follow-bonus (business decision, game-agnostic ACs) — give-away selection must not conflict with it.

## Desired change

1. **Select and document the three give-away games** (business decision; Main Street noted as a candidate; rationale recorded).
2. Define the **trigger config** (achievement ids from CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ's manifest → unlocked game id) in one place (e.g. `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts`).
3. **Extend the shared unlock mechanism** from CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC to accept achievement-triggered unlocks (same persistence/unlock path; new trigger source alongside the follow trigger).
4. **UI:** locked give-away games shown in the Game Selector with unlock progress (which trigger achievements remain); unlocked games become playable.
5. Tests (mocked trigger source + unlock persistence; headless unit tests) + documentation.

## Key Files

- `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts` (new) — give-away config: trigger achievement ids → game id; selection rationale comment.
- `electron/` unlock module from CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC — extended with the achievement trigger source (shared path, game-agnostic).
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` (or launcher UI module) — locked state + unlock progress display for give-away games.
- Achievement manifest from CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ — the trigger ids referenced by the config.
- `tests/` — unit tests for trigger evaluation and unlock persistence with mocked sources.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md` — give-away configuration and QA workflow documentation.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC – Follow-on-Steam incentive: unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher** (open, intake_complete) — the unlock mechanism this item reuses; its open question on the follow-bonus game choice must be coordinated with give-away selection.
- **CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ – Challenges as achievements: sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements** (open, idea) — the engine-generic achievement event source; blocked-by for this item.
- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, plan_complete) — the Steam version hosting both features.
- `main.ts` GAMES catalog — the candidate pool for the three give-away games.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ and CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC land first; this item's implementation is gated on both.
- **Assumption:** The three give-away games are chosen from the current catalog; Main Street is a candidate (user note).
- **Risk:** Conflict between the follow-on-Steam bonus game and the give-away set (e.g. same game twice, or devaluing the follow incentive) — mitigation: selection and rationale recorded, coordinated with the follow-item's open question.
- **Risk:** If the achievement layer (CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ) is delayed, the trigger source is missing — mitigation: define the trigger config/interface in this item early, independent of Steam sync internals.
- **Scope-creep risk:** trading cards, seasonal give-aways, paid DLC sales, and anti-abuse (achievement-farm detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Do you already have the three games in mind, or should the work item include evaluating/selecting them from the catalog (e.g. Main Street, Golf, Blackjack…)?"
  — Answer (user): "don't know yet (note Main Street)". Source: interactive reply (2026-08-09). Implication: selection is a deliverable of this item; Main Street is a recorded candidate.
- Q2: "Should the give-away unlock on specific milestone achievements (e.g. 'complete all challenges in a game', 'win your first game'), or on any achievement being reached?"
  — Answer (user): "win your first game plus one other (suggest)". Source: interactive reply (2026-08-09). **Suggested second achievement: "win your first game in a second distinct game"** (rewards breadth of play; both triggers are engine-generic and achievable without the give-away game itself). Alternative candidates: "complete your first full game" (reach a game-over screen without quitting) or "complete all challenges in any game". Final choice to be confirmed at planning.
- OPEN QUESTION: Which three games? (business decision; Main Street noted).
- OPEN QUESTION: Final definition of the second trigger achievement (suggestion above; confirm at planning).
data.title: Achievement give-aways: unlock three games when achievements are achieved (reuse follow-on-Steam mechanism)

data.description: Discovered during CG-0MTH9OWF2002YQQ3. The test-skill runner (run_tests.py) resolves suites per repo root; however the --suite node path calls node_suite_commands() WITHOUT the project root (~line 1032), so for TCE it emits the framework repo's node --test tests/node/**/*.mjs commands instead of TCE's vitest suite, returning cached success for the wrong suite. Workaround: --suite all --project-root <repo> resolves npm --silent test correctly. Suggested fix: thread cwd into node_suite_commands() and/or add .pi/test-config.json suiteCommands for TCE. discovered-from:CG-0MTH9OWF2002YQQ3

## Goal

Render the merged static + dynamic catalogue in the Game Selector identically, and surface incompatible runtime games to the user as a non-blocking notice.

## Context

Part of FEATURE: Electron runtime game plugin loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5). Realises AC1 (dynamic games appear alongside static ones) and AC4 (incompatible games hidden, presence noted). Producer decision (this session, Q2 = A): incompatible games are **hidden** from the grid and listed in a notice line.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GameSelectorScene` renders dynamic entries through the same card-layout code path as static entries; a game loaded at runtime with a thumbnail renders it using its resolved `tce-games://` URL.
- Incompatible games are absent from the card grid and listed in a visible notice (e.g. `Incompatible game: X — requires core vY.Z`), using SLL/`anchorPoint`-based positioning (no new hardcoded pixel coordinates).
- A dynamic game whose thumbnail fails to load degrades gracefully (text-only card, no exception) — extending the existing `hasThumbnail` guard.
- An empty dynamic catalogue (no `games/` dir) leaves the selector pixel-identical to the current static-only behaviour.
- A browser test covers: merged static+dynamic rendering, the incompatible notice, and missing-thumbnail degradation.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `GameEntry` with optional `incompatible?: { requiredRange: string }` (or pass a separate `incompatibleGames` list into `init`/registry).
- Add a `renderIncompatibleNotice()` helper to `GameSelectorScene` and route thumbnail URLs through `image.setTexture`/loader using already-resolved URLs.
- Browser test in `tests/ui/game-selector-plugin.browser.test.ts`.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts`
- `tests/ui/game-selector-plugin.browser.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- F4 dynamic ESM import & scene registration.

## Goal

Wire the plugin loader into the Electron launcher boot path: await dynamic game discovery before Phaser boots, register discovered scenes, seed the merged catalogue, and degrade gracefully to the static catalogue on any failure.

## Context

Part of FEATURE: Electron runtime game plugin loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5). Realises AC1 (register discovered scenes), AC3 (assets via protocol from F3) and AC4 (graceful degradation). The renderer already receives `window.tce.contentDir` from `electron/preload.cjs`; `main.ts` currently seeds `REGISTRY_KEY_GAMES` synchronously from `virtual:game-registry`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Graceful degradation** — If the manifest is missing, malformed, or a game fails to load, the launcher continues with the statically-registered games and logs an error. Incompatible games are hidden from the selector but their presence is noted (e.g., "Incompatible game: X — requires core vY.Z").
- `main.ts` awaits `loadGamePlugins({ contentDir: window.tce?.contentDir, engineVersion })` **before** `createCardGame(...)`, then registers discovered scene classes and seeds the registry with `{ static: GAMES, dynamic, incompatible }` (or an equivalent merged shape).
- Development / browser (non-Electron) and core-only builds with no `window.tce.contentDir` skip dynamic loading and behave exactly as today.
- **Graceful degradation** — A missing, malformed, or partially-failing manifest logs a clear error and boots the launcher with the static catalogue only — no blank screen, no unhandled rejection.
- `electron/main.ts` registers the `tce-games://` protocol before `createWindow()` and continues to load the renderer via `loadFile`.
- Unit/integration tests cover: no-Electron fallback, malformed manifest fallback, successful merge (appended scenes + entries), and protocol-registration wiring (via injectable/testable seams).

## Minimal Implementation

- Update `main.ts` to an async bootstrap: resolve contentDir, await loader, merge, register scenes, seed registry.
- Update `electron/main.ts` to register the F3 protocol.
- Split the merge/registration logic into a small pure helper (`buildGameBootPayload`) for testability.
- Tests in `tests/ui/game-plugin-boot.test.ts` and `tests/electron/launcher-protocol.browser.test.ts` (or unit where feasible).

## Key Files

- `main.ts`
- `electron/main.ts`
- `src/ui/GamePluginLoader.ts`
- `tests/ui/game-plugin-boot.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- F3 asset resolution & `tce-games://` protocol.
- F4 dynamic ESM import & scene registration.
- F5 Game Selector merge & incompatible notice.

## Goal

Deliver a minimal reference builder that turns a game's source into a loadable runtime artifact (ESM entry + assets + manifest entry), defining the contract every `tce-<game>` repo will follow.

## Context

Part of FEATURE: Electron runtime game plugin loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5). No Vite library-mode game build exists today; without it the loader's end-to-end AC cannot be demonstrated with a real game. Scope is deliberately minimal: one script + docs, not a full per-game release pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `scripts/build-game-artifact.mjs` builds one game (via `--game <id>` / the selected preset entry) in Vite library mode into `build/game-artifacts/<id>/`, emitting an ESM `entry.js`.
- The build externalises `phaser` and the `@core-engine/*`, `@card-system/*`, `@rule-engine/*`, `@ui/*`, `@ai/*` aliases so the artifact does not bundle a second Phaser/engine copy (verified by asserting those specifiers are absent from the emitted bundle and importing them at runtime from the launcher).
- The emitted artifact re-exports the game's scene class and `GAME_INFO` in a shape the loader consumes, and copies its declared thumbnail asset into `assets/`.
- The script can emit or merge a `manifest.json` entry (id, sceneKey, title, description, thumbnail, coreEngineVersion, entry) for the built game.
- A test builds a fixture game (or golf) and asserts the artifact loads through `loadGamePlugins` with a stubbed importer.
- The build output directory is gitignored and does not dirty the working tree.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `scripts/build-game-artifact.mjs` (Vite `build.lib`, `rollupOptions.external`).
- Add an npm script `build:game-artifact`.
- Add `tests/scripts/build-game-artifact.test.ts` (or a focused smoke script).
- Update `.gitignore` for `build/game-artifacts/`.

## Key Files

- `scripts/build-game-artifact.mjs`
- `package.json`
- `.gitignore`
- `tests/scripts/build-game-artifact.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- F4 dynamic ESM import & scene registration.

## Goal

Verify the complete runtime plugin flow end-to-end in the packaged Electron launcher — the acceptance gate for the parent feature's AC1–AC4.

## Context

Part of FEATURE: Electron runtime game plugin loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5). This is the dedicated verification slice; it consumes the builder (F7) and the boot wiring (F6). Because the Electron runtime is not covered by the standard browser suite, this item records a repeatable runbook plus scripted checks where feasible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Full project test suite must pass** with the loader present (no regression for build-time presets).
- With a real artifact dropped into `<contentDir>/games/` plus a valid `manifest.json`, launching `npm run start:electron` shows the game in the Game Selector alongside static games, and it is playable.
- With an incompatible `coreEngineVersion`, the game is hidden and the incompatibility notice names the game and required range.
- With `games/manifest.json` missing or malformed, the launcher boots and lists only the static games; an error is logged.
- The same three scenarios are exercised by an automated check (browser/unit harness with the loader + a stub host where a full Electron launch is impractical), and the packaged runbook documents the manual steps and expected observations.
- Evidence (commands, observed output/notes) is recorded on the work item; the verification is repeatable using only committed scripts/docs.

- **Full project test suite passes** with the loader present (no regression for build-time presets): the unit/browser suites run green at the verification commit.

- Add a runbook under `docs/dev/` or the work-item comment describing the three packaged scenarios.

- Record results as a work-item comment.

## Key Files

- `tests/ui/game-plugin-e2e.test.ts`
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- `scripts/build-game-artifact.mjs`

## Dependencies

- F6 Electron boot wiring & graceful degradation.
- F7 reference game artifact builder.

## Goal

Fix the shared `HandView` so that, when `maxSlots` is set, card and outline positions derive from the hand's **capacity** rather than the current card count — adding a card never moves an existing card or slot.

## Context

Parent: CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ. Sibling test items add the failing unit and browser tests first.

Root cause: `computeCardPositions()` builds a row centred on `this.cards.length` (`layoutCardPositions({ count: this.cards.length, … })`), and `_computeOutlineSlots()` ghosts it (plus appending extras). The empty-hand branch already lays out the desired fixed `maxSlots` row, so that row is the template to reuse. `getInsertionPosition()`, `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, and the animated `sortCards` path all re-derive the row/rotation normalisation from the occupied positions and must move to the template as well. `setMaxSlots()` currently only rebuilds outlines and does not re-lay the cards.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC1–AC5: implement the capacity-template behaviour — outline slot positions identical for a hand of 0…`maxSlots` cards; `addCard` fills the next slot right of the occupied run while pre-existing card positions are unchanged; occupied outlines still match card `x/y/rotation` with extras below every card; `setMaxSlots(n)` is the only mutation that re-lays the row and always yields exactly `n` slots; the empty-hand capacity row is unchanged (same centred straight/arc row the cards will occupy).
- Add a shared private helper in `src/ui/HandView.ts` that derives the `maxSlots` template with the existing `layoutCardPositions` maths (gap = `spacing - cardWidth`, `centerX`, `maxWidth` compression, `arcRadius` Y) and the template-span rotation normalisation; recompute from current options on each use (no stale cache).
- `computeCardPositions()` horizontal returns the first `cards.length` template positions; over-capacity cards continue with the template step to the right (best-effort, no re-centring).
- `getInsertionPosition(index)` returns the template position at `index` (first `maxSlots`; template step beyond), so Market→hand transfer animations land exactly on the resting card.
- `_computeOutlineSlots()` derives all `count` slots from the same template (occupied slots ghost the card's **actual** sprite rotation, extras keep `depth = index - 0.5 - count`), replacing the per-count ghosting/extension branch.
- Rotation and arc normalisation in `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, and the animated `sortCards` path use the template span when `maxSlots` is set, so per-card rotation is also stable across adds.
- `setMaxSlots(maxSlots)` re-lays the cards (calls `applyLayout()`), not just the outlines.
- Capacity-driven layout is keyed on `maxSlots !== undefined`, independent of `showPositionOutlines`; toggling outlines never moves cards.
- Hands without `maxSlots` keep the existing centred-on-count layout; vertical cascade keeps `baseY + i * spacing` and is not regressed.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` is reused unchanged.
- The sibling unit and browser test items pass (`npx vitest run --project unit tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts`).

**Key Files:**

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — `computeCardPositions()`, `_computeOutlineSlots()`, `getInsertionPosition()`, `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, `sortCards()` animated path, `setMaxSlots()`.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` — reused to build the capacity row (no change expected).

**Deliverables:**

- Capacity-driven `HandView` layout with stable card and outline slots and green sibling tests.

## Goal

Verify the complete change set end-to-end and make the parent audit-ready (parent AC9).

## Context

Parent: CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ. Final verification item; depends on the implementation and docs siblings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC9: full project test suite must pass with the new changes — `/skill:test` (quiet mode, triaged) green at the commit under review, which populates the per-repo audit test cache.
- `npm run build` succeeds (TypeScript compile + Vite bundle).
- Unit profile (`npm test -- --project unit`) green.
- Smoke and dev profiles (`npm run test:smoke`, `npm run test:dev`) green.
- Main Street browser suite (including the market→hand click/drag/transfer paths that read `getInsertionPosition`) green, confirming the `handCenterX` anchoring/transfer risk did not materialise.

# Feature: Ship the ToneForge runtime synth module everywhere (commit it)

## Goal (user story)

As a player/tester running TCE in **any** environment — the launcher dev server,
a game-repo dev server, the built `dist/` (GitHub Pages), or the Electron
bundle — Main Street's ToneForge-backed synthesis audio works out of the box,
without anyone having to install the `tf` CLI or run `npm run tf:generate`
first.

## Context

Today the runtime synth module is generated on demand and never shipped:

- `scripts/tf-generate-synths.sh` writes `build/tf-synths/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs`
  (and a metadata module + WAVs + JSON) and **hard-fails** (`exit 1`) if the
  `tf` CLI is not on `PATH`.
- `build/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:15`) and Vite only copies `public/` into
  `dist/`, so the artefact is reachable on the dev server (which serves
  repo-root files) but **absent from `dist/` and the Electron bundle**.
- The runtime pre-checks `/build/tf-synths/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` and,
  when missing, logs `[MainStreet] ToneForge synth module not found …`
  (`src/tf/mainStreetTfModule.ts`).
- The decision recorded in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (§ToneForge Audio Generation) and
  `docs/the-build/audio.md` is explicitly **"we do not commit generated tf
  artifacts"** — this work item reverses that for the runtime module.
- CI never installs ToneForge, so generating at build time cannot work there.

The generated runtime module is **static JavaScript** (hard-coded Tone.js
factories) whose only runtime dependency is `tone`, which is already a shipped
dependency. It therefore does not need `tf`, WAVs, or network access at runtime.

## Proposed approach (confirm during planning)

1. Make the generated **runtime synth module** a source-controlled artefact so
   it is present in every checkout and copied into every build. Likely:
   generate/commit it at a path the runtime already serves
   (`public/build/tf-synths/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` in the launcher keeps
   the existing `/build/tf-synths/…` URL unchanged), or place it with the
   Main Street game assets and compose it via
   `repo-layout.json → gameAssets` (CG-0MUKYCG9L00587FA), updating the default
   URL.
2. Make `scripts/tf-generate-synths.sh` **fail-open**: a missing `tf` CLI is a
   warning/regeneration hint, never a build failure. `npm run build`/`dev` must
   not depend on `tf` and must not be changed to run generation.
3. Decide what is committed vs generated: commit the runtime module (and
   evaluate the metadata module); keep WAV/JSON generated output out of source
   control.
4. Update the docs to state which artefact is committed and how to regenerate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Clean checkout, no `tf`, no generation:** with the `tf` CLI absent and
   `npm run tf:generate` never run, `GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run dev` serves the
   runtime synth module at the exact URL `loadMainStreetTfModule()` requests,
   Main Street logs **no** `ToneForge synth module not found` warning, and
   synth-mapped SFX are active.
2. **Shipped build:** `GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run build` emits the module into
   `dist/` at the same URL path, and serving `dist/` (e.g. `npm run preview`)
   loads it with no warning. Same for `npm run build:electron`.
3. **Deterministic + single source of truth:** the committed module is the file
   the runtime loads; running `npm run tf:generate` (when `tf` is available)
   regenerates exactly that artefact with no drift, and the absence of `tf`
   never fails `npm run build` or `npm run dev`.
4. **Test coverage:** a unit test asserts the runtime default URL resolves to an
   on-disk artefact that is included in the public/build output, and that the
   module exports `TF_RUNTIME_MODULE`/`factories` including the expected keys
   (`card-draw`, `card-slide`, `card-place`, `card-discard`,
   `card-coin-collect`, `ui-notification-chime`, `card-table-ambience`,
   `construction-hammer`, `construction-saw`, `construction-lite-hammer`,
   `construction-lite-saw`, `crowd-cheer`).
5. **Docs:** `docs/DEVELOPER.md` §ToneForge Audio Generation and
   `docs/the-build/audio.md` no longer claim the runtime module is uncommitted;
   they state which artefact is source-controlled and how to regenerate it.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- Committing WAV or JSON generation output (binary/large) is out of scope.
- If the module must also be present in the **standalone `tce-main-street`
  repo**, that is a cross-repo follow-up; record it as a child/spin-off if the
  chosen placement does not cover it.

## Related

- Reverses the "do not commit generated tf artifacts" decision in
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` / `docs/the-build/audio.md`.
- Prior work: CG-0MOIY2VV200658OX (TF output spike + spec, open questions #2/#4),
  CG-0MOIY3MSR008EH0I (npm script + docs), CG-0MOIXHOWP003Y6E0 (runtime
  synthesis).
- Sibling asset composition: CG-0MUKYCG9L00587FA.
- Discovered-from: CG-0MUKYCG9L00587FA.
data.title: Ship the ToneForge runtime synth module everywhere (commit it)

# Documentation gap — stale game paths in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`

**discovered-from:CG-0MUMAIIT40002MRP** (Update AGENTS.md for the split multi-repo structure and cross-repo change guidance)

## Problem

`docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents the **merged core checkout** (`Tableau-Card-Engine`) but still lists example-game paths as `example-games/<game>/…` for games that now live in sibling `tce-<game>` repos at repo-root `src/`. This was discovered while correcting the equivalent stale paths in `AGENTS.md`; it is out of scope for that item (which is bounded to `AGENTS.md` + the context-budget threshold).

## Evidence

`grep -nE 'example-games/(golf|blackjack|coloretto|main-street|sushi-go|feudalism|lost-cities|beleaguered-castle)' docs/DEVELOPER.md` returns roughly 40 non-Gym references, including:

- **Game reference table** — `example-games/golf/`, `example-games/main-street/`, `example-games/beleaguered-castle/`, etc.
- **Hand & Pile Rendering** — `example-games/golf/scenes/GolfRenderer.ts`, `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts`.
- **Animation & Sound Feedback** — `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoAiScheduler.ts`, `example-games/golf/scenes/GolfAnimator.ts`, `example-games/blackjack/scenes/BlackjackScene.ts`.
- **SLL layout table / Main Street asset generation / Renderer migration / tutorial paths** — further `example-games/main-street/…` references.

The multi-repo note at the top of the *Project Structure* section already states the core carries no games at HEAD and that each game lives at repo-root `src/`, so the file is internally contradictory.

## Desired change

Repoint every non-Gym game path in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` to the sibling layout (`../tce-<game>/src/…`), or to the game repo's own documented layout where the reference is game-repo-relative. Gym references (`example-games/gym/…`) stay unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `grep -nE 'example-games/(golf|blackjack|coloretto|main-street|sushi-go|feudalism|lost-cities|beleaguered-castle)' docs/DEVELOPER.md` returns no matches; remaining `example-games/` references are Gym-only or structural.
2. No code/behaviour change (docs only).
3. Build and the unit test profile pass.
4. Relevant doc cross-links (e.g. `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`, `README.md`) remain consistent.

## Constraints

- Docs-only change; write UK English; no new top-level doc structure.

## Goal

As a distribution operator, I want the CI-built Windows installer
(`TCE-Setup-<version>.exe` from the `Package Windows Binary` workflow) promoted to
a GitHub Release automatically as part of the release process, so I do not have
to remember to run `/skill:release-windows` manually after every `dev`→`main`
release.

## Context

- `.github/workflows/package.yml` builds the installer on push to `main` and on
  tag `v*`, smoke-tests the packaged binary, and uploads it as the
  `tce-windows-installer` workflow artifact — but it never calls `gh release
  create`, so no GitHub Release is produced automatically.
- `.pi/skills/release-windows/` (CG-0MSQ6MV7N0085V9R, completed) is the
  **manual** path: it promotes the latest successful artifact to a **draft**
  GitHub Release with `CHANGELOG.md` notes, and the operator publishes the draft.
- `/skill:ship release` bumps the version, creates/pushes the tag `v<semver>`
  (ancestor of `origin/main`) and merges `dev`→`main`, then verifies the tag
  before closing work items.
- Gap: the promotion is agent-invoked and easy to miss; a release can ship the
  Pages site + workflow artifact while the GitHub Release never appears.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Automatic promotion** — After `dev`→`main` is released (tag `v*` pushed),
  the Windows installer is promoted to a GitHub Release with no manual skill
  invocation.
- **Draft, not published** — The created release is a **draft** (operator
  publishes it in the GitHub UI). It attaches `TCE-Setup-<version>.exe`, uses the
  matching `CHANGELOG.md` section as release notes (falling back to
  `--generate-notes` when absent), and reuses the existing `v<version>` tag —
  never overwriting an existing release or tag.
- **Idempotent** — Re-running promotion for a version that already has a release
  is a no-op that reports the existing release URL.
- **Non-blocking failure** — A failed promotion (no successful
  `Package Windows Binary` run, missing artifact, missing/insufficient `gh`
  auth) does not fail the Pages deploy and is surfaced with a clear message
  (workflow annotation / job summary).
- **Single source of truth for the version** — The release version is derived
  from the installer filename / `package.json` (`electron-builder.yml`
  `artifactName`), consistent with the existing `release-windows` helper.
- **Tests** — The promotion logic is covered by automated tests (workflow
  dry-run and/or unit tests around the promotion helper); the existing
  `tests/release-windows/` suite continues to pass.
- **Documentation updated** — `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (packaging/release section)
  and the release-process docs state that the GitHub Release is produced
  automatically; the `release-windows` skill is updated to reflect the
  automated path while remaining the documented manual fallback.

## Out of scope

- Linux/macOS binary promotion (Windows only, as today).
- Steam upload integration.
- Auto-**publishing** releases (the draft remains the operator approval gate).

## Assumptions

- Interpreted as **automating/integrating** the existing promotion into the
  release pipeline rather than a one-off manual promotion. If a one-off was
  intended, this item can be closed by running `/skill:release-windows` on the
  current version.
- Draft (not published) remains the correct approval model, matching the
  existing skill.
data.title: Automate promotion of the CI-built Windows installer to a GitHub Release

## Summary

Add a Steam-free achievement layer to the core engine, extending the generic `ChallengeSystem` model: achievement definitions, a declarative challenge-to-achievement mapping, an idempotent unlock registry, and a pluggable `AchievementSink`. It works headless and in the web build, where the sink is a no-op local record.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts` defines `AchievementDefinition` (id, title, description, hidden), an `AchievementManifest` (game id plus challenge-to-achievement mapping), an `AchievementSink`, and an `AchievementSystem` that maps challenge completions to achievement unlocks.
- [ ] Unlocks are idempotent: a repeated completion of the same challenge or achievement sinks exactly once per session, and re-registering an already-unlocked achievement is a no-op.
- [ ] The layer has zero Steam or Electron imports and is exported from `src/core-engine/index.ts`; a headless/browser run works with a no-op sink.
- [ ] It integrates with the existing generic `ChallengeCompletionCallback` so a game can wire challenge completion to an achievement unlock without game-specific Steam code.
- [ ] Unit tests cover definitions validation, mapping resolution, idempotent unlock, hidden-flag propagation, unmapped challenges, and sink-dispatch failure tolerance; they pass under `--project unit`.

## Minimal Implementation

- New `AchievementSystem.ts` plus a barrel export in `src/core-engine/index.ts`.
- Reuse the `ChallengeSystem.ts` completion callback surface instead of duplicating challenge evaluation.
- Keep an in-memory unlock registry with an injectable persistence seed (already-unlocked ids) so the launcher can rehydrate it.

## Summary

Add the launcher-side single source of truth for achievements and a pure-Node, idempotent, offline-safe sync service behind the `AchievementSource` interface. The service persists unlocked achievements locally and re-syncs them to Steam when available, and never throws when Steam is absent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `electron/achievement-manifest.json` and a typed loader define the single source of truth: game id to achievement id to Steam API name to hidden flag; a missing or invalid manifest degrades to `null` with no crash.

- [ ] Mismatch detection is implemented and documented: unknown achievement ids, duplicate or non-matching Steam API names, and manifest/store drift surface a clear, non-fatal diagnostic.

## Summary

Document the achievement architecture and workflow (engine layer, manifest as source of truth, Steam bridge, graceful degradation) and provide a documented manual end-to-end check with a real Steam account, as required by the intake acceptance criteria.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/dev/steam-achievements-qa.md` documents a manual E2E plan with a real Steam account (the unlock appears in the Steam overlay and profile; offline then re-sync; the absent-Steam fallback) with Pass/Fail and evidence steps.
- [ ] `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents the achievement layer: the manifest format and the requirement that it matches the Steam store backend (API names and hidden flags), the challenge-to-achievement mapping workflow for a new game, and the no-Steam-SDK-in-game rule.
- [ ] `./README.md` and the relevant `./AGENTS.md` sections reference the achievement layer and the manifest; the new modules carry explanatory comments.
- [ ] The manifest-to-Steam-store mismatch detection procedure is documented (what to check, where, and how to fix drift).
- [ ] Documentation is reviewed against the shipped code paths so every referenced file and API exists.

## Minimal Implementation

- Follow `docs/dev/steam-follow-qa.md` as the template for the QA plan.
- Update `./README.md`, `./AGENTS.md`, and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` in the same commit as the doc changes.

## Dependencies

- F5: Real Steamworks achievement adapter.
- F6: Achievement IPC bridge and renderer client.
- F7: Main Street first consumer.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/dev/steam-achievements-qa.md`
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- `./AGENTS.md`
- `./README.md`

## Deliverables

- Manual E2E QA plan and developer documentation updates.
